content.value_statement: Static interfaces can feel abrupt and unclear during state changes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to add accessible, performant motion where it improves usability.
actual_capabilities: Reviews a feature or component for useful animation opportunities.
Plans entrance, feedback, transition, navigation, and guidance animations.
Recommends timing ranges and easing curves for common UI motion.
Prioritizes transform and opacity animations for smoother performance.
Defines quality checks for frame rate, timing, interaction, and purpose.
limitations: Requires project context before animation choices can be reliable.
Does not include runnable implementation files or reusable animation components.
Depends on another frontend-design skill for broader design guidance.
Provides guidance, not automated performance measurement.

use_cases.title: Polish Product Workflows
use_cases.description: Add subtle feedback and transitions to forms, dashboards, and repeated actions without distracting users.

use_cases.title: Improve Frontend Components
use_cases.description: Identify buttons, modals, tabs, and loading states that need clearer motion and feedback.

use_cases.title: Audit Motion Accessibility
use_cases.description: Check that animations respect reduced-motion preferences and avoid tiring or blocking interactions.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused animation review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the animate skill to review this component and suggest purposeful micro-interactions that improve feedback and clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Motion For A Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a workflow-level animation plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the animate skill to create an animation plan for this user flow, including entrance, feedback, and state transitions.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Accessible Motion
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that asks for implementation guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the animate skill to add accessible animations to this feature, with reduced-motion support and performance constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Refine A Motion System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for consistent product-wide motion guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the animate skill to audit this interface and define consistent timing, easing, and interaction rules for its motion system.

output_examples.input: Review a settings modal for animation opportunities.
output: The modal should fade and slide in quickly, with focus moving into the dialog.
Primary buttons need a short press response, while validation messages should appear with a gentle transition.
Reduced-motion users should receive instant state changes without decorative movement.

output_examples.input: Improve tab switching in a dashboard.
output: Use a sliding tab indicator to preserve spatial context between sections.
Fade content changes within a short duration so repeated switching remains fast.
Avoid parallax or long transitions because dashboard users need efficient scanning.

output_examples.input: Audit a page load animation for quality.
output: Keep the main reveal under 800ms and stagger secondary content in small increments.
Animate transform and opacity only, then verify smooth behavior on target devices.
Confirm the experience still works when reduced-motion preferences are enabled.

best_practices: Start with audience, use case, brand tone, and performance constraints before adding motion.
Use animation to clarify feedback, state changes, hierarchy, or navigation.
Always support reduced-motion preferences and verify performance on target devices.
anti_patterns: Adding animation everywhere without a clear user benefit.
Using long feedback animations that make the interface feel slow.
Animating layout properties when transform or opacity can achieve the effect.

faq.question: What does this skill help animate?
faq.answer: It helps improve components, flows, state changes, loading states, modals, navigation, and micro-interactions.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides implementation guidance and may guide edits, but the skill itself is instruction-only.

faq.question: How does it handle accessibility?
faq.answer: It requires reduced-motion alternatives and warns against motion that blocks or exhausts users.

faq.question: Which technologies does it mention?
faq.answer: It references CSS transitions, keyframes, Web Animations API, Framer Motion, and GSAP.

faq.question: Is it suitable for serious business software?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes purposeful motion, restraint, performance, and user context before visual delight.

faq.question: What should users provide before using it?
faq.answer: Users should provide the target feature, audience, use case, brand tone, and performance constraints when available.
